pl-l2d27c2-d1e108.summary: Asks how prevenient grace merits increase when no merit is without free choice, what grace is, whether a virtue, and if so whether an act.
claims: No merit is without free choice.

pl-l2d27c2-d1e111.summary: States that to answer, it must first be laid down that there are three kinds of goods.

pl-l2d27c2.summary: Raises further questions: how prevenient grace can merit increase when no merit exists without free choice, what this grace is, whether a virtue, and if a virtue, whether an act. To answer, it must first be laid down that there are three kinds of goods.
claims: No merit exists without free choice.
Whether prevenient grace is a virtue, and whether a virtue is an act, must be settled.
The answer begins from three kinds of goods.
